unavailable_fields.pcie_bytes: No per-collective hardware byte counters: capabilities list pcie_bytes as unknown because hardware counters require a successful collector-specific probe; topology and logical payload do not measure traffic. device_telemetry provides device-wide NVML rates with native sampling windows only, and traffic must not be invented from logical payload or memcpy sizes.
unavailable_fields.nvlink_bytes: Hardware byte counters unavailable for the same probe reason; observed NCCL transport is SHM/direct/direct with peer_access.0.1=0 and peer_access.1.0=0, so no NVLink P2P path is in use to attribute bytes to.
unavailable_fields.hardware_utilization: Listed unknown in capabilities; hardware counters require a successful collector-specific probe; only device-wide NVML utilization samples with device-dependent, unaligned windows are available.
unavailable_fields.per_collective.wait_vs_wire_ms: Nsys timelines alone do not separate NCCL waiting from wire transfer, and no cross-rank timestamp subtraction is permitted; only bounded attribution is possible by combining the joint nsys timeline with the correctness-checked collective_calibration reference at observed sizes/dtypes.
unavailable_fields.bucket_identity.exact_links: Each 28351488-byte allreduce retains 12 same-size bucket candidates; exact bucket-to-collective links require native correlation and observed gradient-storage membership. The passive bucket inventory does not allocate collective cost, no communication hook is installed, and execution_timeline never replaces one, so ambiguous candidates are retained.
unavailable_fields.submission.gpu_readiness_and_consumer_co: execution_timeline reports clock alignment bounds for matching CPU submissions only; GPU readiness and consumer completion for those submissions may remain unknown.

plan.rationale: Objective is diagnostic.max_rank_nccl_kernel_sum_ms (max-rank NCCL kernel time). The completed torch run observed all 13 cross-rank-matched allreduces (12x 28351488 B buckets + the 157541376 B is_last bucket, 13/13 payload coverage, no unmatched comm kernels) with rank0 sum 281.2 ms vs rank1 63.4 ms, first rank0 kernel 101.6 ms vs 3.6 ms on rank1, near-zero compute overlap (6.9/7.8 ms), and symmetric ~19.5 ms on the final large bucket. The open question for the objective is whether rank0's extra kernel time is peer-arrival wait, launch/readiness skew, or SHM/direct/direct (peer access disabled) wire time; cross-rank clock subtraction is prohibited, so this cannot be settled from the torch trace alone. nsys is available and runs separately on a joint aligned timeline to resolve overlap and attribution (cross-rank NCCL kernel vs compute overlap, NCCL API enqueue/launch correlation); it is understood that nsys alone does not separate waiting from wire transfer or prove bucket identity. execution_timeline adds CPU-to-CUDA submit associations, synchronization, per-device intervals and passive gradient post-accumulate callbacks to locate submit skew and gradient-readiness ordering, with clock alignment bounds for matching CPU submissions only and no role in driving later search actions. collective_calibration runs a correctness-checked synthetic full-world SUM allreduce at the observed sizes/dtypes as a reference for wait-vs-wire scaling, not a lower bound or critical-path estimate. device_telemetry samples available NVML PCIe rates and utilization during the window as device-wide corroboration of interconnect activity, not per-collective bytes. python_runtime is not selected because host dispatch is not implicated by current evidence and its perturbation would confound timing; candidate_diagnostics is not needed for these gaps; torch is not repeated since it already ran.
